title: Rapid Samples Sprint — triage + microtasks (standup notes)
content:
Context: quick follow-up after the Rapid Samples sprint (3 days) — this doc is the triage dump from today's standup and the microtask assignment for the week. Mostly action items and lightweight notes.

Attendees: Priya, Evan, Maya, Liam, Sofia, Jordan (guest, platform tooling)
Time: 2025-09-11 10:00am PT (30m)
Location: Zoom / #devexp-playground

Agenda:
- Quick status on sample templates & failure modes seen during smoke runs
- Which quickstarts can ship as-is, which need docs updates, which need small SDK fixes
- Triage backlog -> create microtasks (<= 2 days each) and owners
- Decide rollback / holdlist for any samples that flaked in CI

Notes / Observations:
- Smoke run (5 core quickstarts) surfaced three classes of problems: auth example out-of-date, streaming response example incomplete, and one flaky GitHub Actions job that times out intermittently.
- New `samples/llm-chat-tooling` example is high-value but currently references the old `client.streaming()` signatures. Needs minimal SDK change or doc shim.
- Quickstart telemetry hook (sample-run metrics) failed for runs that used `--local-cache` flag — likely an env var assumption (DEVEXP_TELEMETRY_PATH).
- We saw inconsistent error messages from the Python SDK when model fallback occurred — user-facing wording needs to be clearer (mentioning fallback variant + link to docs).

Decisions:
- Ship 3 quickstarts this week: "getting-started-node", "embeddings-minimal", "llm-basics-python". These are green after small fixes.
- Put "llm-chat-tooling" on hold until either SDK shim is merged or we add a compatibility note in the README. Prefer shim if <= 4h.
- Disable the flaky CI job in sample repo temporarily and open a fix ticket for infra team (tag: infra-ci).

Action items (owner — estimate — due):
- Evan Liu — fix Python SDK fallback error wording + add link to fallback docs (1d) — due 2025-09-12. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/pull/981 (WIP).
- Maya Gomez — update getting-started-node quickstart README to reflect new API signature for function calling; add one-liner snippet for streaming (3h) — due 2025-09-12.
- Liam O'Connor — create compatibility shim for client.streaming() alias in JS SDK (4h) OR add README compatibility section if longer; start with shim attempt (4h) — due 2025-09-12. PR candidate: https://github.com/redwood-inference/js-sdk/pull/411.
- Sofia Patel — patch telemetry env var handling in samples runner (2h) and write a short note in troubleshooting section (0.5h) — due 2025-09-12. Ticket: JIRA-ENG-2345.
- Priya Raman — toggle off flaky GH action (temporary) and open infra ticket for root cause (0.5h) — done 2025-09-11. Ticket: CONFLUENCE-DEVEXP-615 (tracking doc).
- Jordan (platform) — check whether GH Actions runners in eu-west1 have disk I/O throttling; sync with infra (2d) — due 2025-09-13.

Microtask backlog (prioritized):
1) docs: add explicit fallback section to SDK docs with example messages and remediation steps (owner: Evan)
2) samples: add compatibility note to llm-chat-tooling README and label with "hold-until-shim" (owner: Priya)
3) quickstarts: validate token/credentials flow for embeddings-minimal across mac/linux (owner: Maya)
4) playground: add a smoke test that runs short streaming example and asserts chunked output (owner: Liam)
5) infra: investigate intermittent GH Action timeouts (owner: Jordan / infra), add watchers to failed runs (owner: Priya)

Risks / Open Qs:
- If js-sdk shim takes >1d, shipping llm-chat-tooling will require a poor UX workaround (large README note). Decision threshold: if shim >8h, we add README note and schedule shim for next sprint.
- Telemetry env leak: we need to confirm no customer secrets are written to sample logs when telemetry fails. Action: Sofia to validate logs.
- Are we comfortable with shipping quickstarts that mention streaming but only have a stub example? Team agreed shipping with a stub + clear "streaming: experimental" banner is OK for now.

Short-term checklist (what to verify before merging):
- [ ] sample README updated with exact code snippet and expected output
- [ ] CI: sample smoke test passes locally and on containerized runner (no timeouts)
- [ ] SDK docs: fallback section linked and reviewed by eng-apis
- [ ] PR contains changelog blurb and sample author sign-off

Notes to self / reminders:
- follow up with eng-apis on the wording for fallback (prefer non-technical phrasing for user readability)
- add a quickstart label to PR titles for easier filtering (e.g., [quickstart])
- capture a short 2-min video of the streaming example for internal playbook — will help with support triage if users report confusion

Quicklinks referenced in call:
- samples repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/samples (see /quickstarts and /templates)
- ticket tracker: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/JIRA-ENG-2345
- convo: slack thread #devexp-playground (ts=1694300000)

Next check-in: 2025-09-12 9:30am PT (short standup) — we'll reassign any items that are blocked.

End of notes.

Raw scratch fragments from meeting (keep for context):
- "maybe we should use a tiny test model for streaming smoke tests, reduces flakiness"
- "embedding quickstart fails on python3.9 venv created by CI image"
- "PR template for quickstarts should include 'test matrix' checkbox"
- "drop-in examples for common frameworks (next.js, flask) would help adoption"
